headline: Dry and warming through Thanksgiving, when offshore winds push Glendale and the other coastal valleys into the mid 70s to low 80s, before a cooler weekend and light rain on Sunday; at the beaches, a big swell and very high tides bring coastal flooding and high surf Wednesday and Thursday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Monday was quiet, with highs in the mid to upper 60s in the Los Angeles-area valleys and southern coasts and 50s to low 60s inland and north of Point Conception. Tonight stays dry, with no low clouds expected at the coast or around Glendale and Burbank, as light offshore (northeasterly, Santa Ana-type) winds develop and strengthen into Tuesday morning; they should stay below advisory levels, though the Santa Susana Mountains, San Gabriel Mountains and parts of the Ventura County mountains could see gusts of 30 to 35 mph at times. It will be cold overnight in some spots, with a Freeze Warning in effect for part of the area until 8 AM Tuesday, and very low clouds or dense fog are expected around Paso Robles late tonight into early Tuesday morning.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: The offshore winds and a building area of high pressure warm things up 5 to 10 degrees on Tuesday, with gusts around 30 mph from Santa Clarita and the nearby mountains through the Highway 126 corridor into the Oxnard plain and the northwest San Fernando Valley. A weak cold front approaches from the northwest Tuesday night into early Wednesday, but the latest detailed models show its showers struggling to reach the coast, so any rain, mainly in San Luis Obispo County, would be very light and the chance may be lowered further; clouds cover most of the area Tuesday night into early Wednesday, then Wednesday turns sunny with temperatures similar to Tuesday. Stronger offshore winds bring significant warming on Thanksgiving Thursday, with highs in the mid 70s to low 80s across the coasts and coastal valleys, including the Glendale area, while higher valleys and the interior stay cooler; winds in the usual wind-prone areas could reach low-end advisory levels.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Friday stays warm and dry, and dry weather continues at least through Saturday, but temperatures cool over the weekend, especially at the coast and in the valleys, as winds turn onshore ahead of the next storm. That storm moves through mostly on Sunday, bringing at least some light rain to most areas: up to an inch on the Central Coast, especially its northern part, and likely under half an inch south of Point Conception, including Los Angeles County. At least one more storm is expected around next Tuesday, with 1 to 3 inches possible on mountain slopes facing the incoming storm.

coast: A large, long-period west swell arrives Tuesday and peaks Wednesday and Thursday, combining with very high tides to bring significant surf and significant coastal flooding, which makes for problematic beach weather despite the warmth. The worst is expected on the Central Coast and Ventura County beaches, with somewhat smaller but still concerning issues elsewhere: many strong rip currents nearly everywhere, strong along-shore currents, a risk of sneaker waves, heavy shore break, beach erosion and possible breaking waves at harbor entrances. For the San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara Central Coast beaches, a Coastal Flood Advisory and High Surf Advisory run until 6 AM Wednesday, followed by a Coastal Flood Warning and High Surf Warning from 6 AM Wednesday to noon Thursday. Ventura County beaches have a Coastal Flood Advisory until 8 AM Wednesday and a High Surf Advisory from 9 PM Tuesday to 8 AM Wednesday, then a Coastal Flood Warning and High Surf Warning from 8 AM Wednesday to noon Thursday. The Malibu coast and Los Angeles County beaches have a Coastal Flood Advisory until 8 AM Wednesday, a Coastal Flood Watch from Wednesday morning through Thursday morning, and a High Surf Advisory from 6 AM Wednesday to 9 PM Thursday; the Santa Barbara south coast beaches and islands have a Coastal Flood Advisory until noon Thursday and a High Surf Advisory from 6 AM Wednesday to noon Thursday (to 9 PM Thursday for the islands). For boaters, winds and seas stay below small craft advisory levels through Tuesday afternoon. Small Craft Advisories run from 9 PM Tuesday (3 AM Wednesday for some waters) to 3 PM Thursday, with seas peaking at 14 to 18 feet on the outer waters Wednesday and Wednesday night and 13 to 16 feet north of Point Sal Wednesday. South of Point Conception, there is a 50 to 60 percent chance of advisory-level winds (30 to 40 percent for seas) in the western Santa Barbara Channel Wednesday and a 50 to 70 percent chance of advisory-level northeast winds (40 to 60 percent for seas) from Ventura to Santa Monica Thursday. Friday and Saturday bring lighter winds, though seas could stay at advisory levels on the outer waters (60 to 80 percent chance) and north of Point Sal (40 to 60 percent).
watch_for: Thanksgiving offshore winds possibly reaching low-end advisory levels around Santa Clarita, the Highway 126 corridor, the Oxnard plain and the northwest San Fernando Valley.
Coastal flood and high surf warnings Wednesday into Thursday, worst on the Central Coast and Ventura County beaches, with a Coastal Flood Watch for Los Angeles County beaches.
Rain totals with Sunday's storm and another possible storm around next Tuesday.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in the dry, warming stretch through Saturday and may trim the already small chance of rain Tuesday night, while the Sunday and next-Tuesday storms carry the usual uncertainty in rain amounts.
